# Vendored crates

| Crate | Upstream | License |
|---|---|---|
| `vte` 0.15.0 | [alacritty/vte](https://github.com/alacritty/vte) | Apache-2.0 or MIT |
| `alacritty_terminal` 0.26.0 | [alacritty/alacritty](https://github.com/alacritty/alacritty) | Apache-2.0 |

Both started as the crates.io packages and are wired in by
`[patch.crates-io]` in the workspace `Cargo.toml`; each is its own workspace
(`exclude = ["vendor"]`) and builds into `target/vendor` under the gates.
`alacritty_terminal` depends on the vendored `vte` by path.

## Why

Shift emulates a VT420 (DA1 level 4) and passes esctest2 with xterm's
expectations, which the upstream crates do not attempt. The additions:

- **vte**: parsing and `Handler` methods for rectangle editing, left/right
  margins, selective erase, protected areas, DEC line sizes, conformance
  levels, the DEC locator, national and DEC supplemental/technical character
  sets, the xterm window operations, special colors and DCS requests
  (DECRQSS, XTGETTCAP, DECRSPS); explicit-versus-omitted parameter tracking;
  X11 color specs including the Xcms device-independent forms (`src/xcms.rs`,
  a port of Xlib's color conversion).
- **alacritty_terminal**: the VT420 state and reports (`src/term/vt420.rs`),
  margin-aware cursor motion, scrolling and editing, protected cells, row
  line attributes, reverse wraparound as xterm 383+, and grapheme-cluster
  widths matching wcwidth (`src/term/width.rs`, tables generated by
  `scripts/gen-width-tables.py`). Upstream bugs fixed on the way: a
  `Storage::swap` that assumed the row layout, the kitty keyboard flags set
  with `CSI = … u` never being reported, and a keyboard-mode stack overflow
  trimming the title stack.

## Rules

- Keep each change covered by the crate's own tests; `scripts/gates.sh` runs
  fmt, clippy and the tests of both crates.
- `crates/shift-pty/src/abs_term.rs` must forward every `Handler` method;
  `every_handler_method_is_forwarded` fails when one is missing.
- Three upstream ref tests are excluded in `alacritty_terminal/tests/ref.rs`
  where Shift deliberately follows xterm instead (see the comment there).
